title: Protocol for fabricating immune-regulatory bone organoids via plant-based bioinks
field: 生命科学·细胞与分子生物学

method_excerpt:
GelMA powder and Laponite nanoclay particles were sterilized under ultraviolet light for 2 h prior to bioink preparation. Three formulations were prepared under aseptic conditions.1) GelMA bioink: 0.5 g of GelMA was dissolved in 5 mL of sterile deionized water containing 0.0125 g of lithium phenyl-2,4,6-trimethylbenzoylphosphinate (LAP) under continuous stirring at 37°C for 2 h to yield a 10 wt % GelMA bioink.
2) GelMA/Laponite bioink: 0.05 g of Laponite nanoclay was added to the 10 wt % GelMA solution and stirred at 37°C for 2 h until a homogeneous suspension was formed (10 wt % GelMA, 1 wt % Laponite).
3) GelMA/Laponite/AV bioink: 0.5 g of GelMA and 0.05 g of Laponite nanoclay were dispersed in 3 mL of sterile deionized water containing 0.0125 g of LAP. After 1 h of stirring at 37°C to ensure complete dispersion of Laponite without air bubbles, 2 mL of pre-prepared sterile Aloe vera gel was added and stirred for an additional 1 h at 37°C (final ratio: 10 wt % GelMA, 1 wt % Laponite, and 40 vol % AV).

Construct architecture was designed in Autodesk 3ds Max as an 8-layer rectangular porous grid (5 mm × 5 mm) with an infill spacing of 1.5 mm and an orthogonal 90° interlayer rotation applied twice. rBMSCs at passage 5 were detached with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA, centrifuged (1000 g, 5 min), and gently resuspended in pre-warmed (37°C) bioinks at a density of 1.0×106 cells/mL. The cell-laden bioink was loaded into a light-shielded cartridge and printed using a low-temperature extrusion bioprinter (Bio-Architect SR) at 8°C. Printing parameters were set to: pneumatic pressure of 0.2–0.3 MPa, printing speed of 4 mm/s, retraction height of 2 mm, and a 21G metal nozzle. Filaments were crosslinked layer-by-layer under 365 nm UV light at 5% intensity (20 mW/cm2) for 10 s per layer, followed by 30 s post-curing to stabilize the construct.

Immediately following printing, construct precursors were transferred into multi-well plates and incubated at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere. Constructs were cultured in growth medium (α-MEM containing 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin) for the first 24 h. The medium was subsequently replaced with osteogenic induction medium consisting of α-MEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 10 mM β-glycerophosphate, 50 μg/mL L-ascorbic acid, and 100 nM dexamethasone. Cultures were maintained under static conditions for up to 28 days, with medium refreshed every 2–3 days.

Following 24 h of Transwell co-culture, RAW 264.7 cells were detached with trypsin-EDTA, washed with PBS, and collected by centrifugation (1000 g, 5 min). Cells were fixed in 4% PFA for 10 min, permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 10 min, and incubated with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-iNOS (1:100) and PE-conjugated anti-CD206 (1:100) antibodies for 30 min. After repeated washing with PBS, cells were analyzed on a flow cytometer to determine the percentages of iNOS+ and CD206+ populations.
blind_brief:
骨类器官是研究骨发育、骨病和骨再生的三维模型。现有体系大多只关注成骨分化和基质生成，很少纳入免疫调控成分，而巨噬细胞从促炎到促再生的表型转换在骨修复中非常关键。另一方面，常用的 Matrigel 来源于小鼠肉瘤，成分复杂且不明确，批次差异大，限制了实验的可重复性和临床转化。本研究提出一种不含 Matrigel、也不添加外源细胞因子的植物基复合生物墨水：甲基丙烯酰化明胶（GelMA）提供可细胞黏附、可光交联的网络，合成纳米黏土 Laponite 用于改善流变性和可打印性，芦荟凝胶（AV）作为潜在的免疫调节组分。

实验设计如下：设置 GelMA、GelMA/Laponite、GelMA/Laponite/AV 三组配方，比较对象为配方组分本身。先以可打印性、丝条保真度、压缩模量和包埋细胞活力为依据，对各组分浓度做多参数权衡筛选。随后将大鼠骨髓间充质干细胞包埋于墨水中，在低温条件下挤出打印并逐层紫外交联，得到骨类器官前体，再进行最长 28 天的成骨诱导培养，评估成骨分化与矿化。免疫方面，通过与 RAW 264.7 巨噬细胞共培养，评估巨噬细胞的迁移、侵袭、黏附及 iNOS/CD206 表型。体内部分包括裸鼠皮下植入实验，以及大鼠颅骨临界尺寸缺损修复实验（观察 4 周和 8 周），并通过主要脏器组织学和血液生化进行生物安全性评估。

review_excerpt:
Laponite nanoclay was incorporated to improve the rheological behavior and structural integrity of the bioink. Its characteristic “house-of-cards” microstructure imparts strong shear-thinning properties, which are particularly advantageous for extrusion-based 3D bioprinting.10 Moreover, Laponite particles exhibit high surface area and excellent dispersibility, contributing to enhanced mechanical strength of the hydrogel composite. Notably, degradation products such as Mg2+ and Si4+ have been shown to create a pro-regenerative microenvironment that supports bone formation, further justifying the inclusion of Laponite in the scaffold formulation to improve printability and augment mechanical properties such as elastic modulus and toughness. AV was incorporated as the immune-regulatory component. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis identified multiple small-molecule constituents, including phytosphingosine- and polyphenol-related metabolites, while AV is also known to contain bioactive polysaccharides such as acemannan. These constituents may contribute to macrophage regulation and tissue repair.11 Unlike approaches that rely on exogenous cytokines such as IL-4, the AV-containing bioink produced sustained macrophage recruitment and pro-regenerative polarization in the original study.12,13 Bulk RNA-seq revealed broad immune remodeling involving Th1/Th2/Th17-related pathways and alterations associated with STAT6, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and RANKL-related signaling. These findings are consistent with enhanced pro-regenerative responses and reduced inflammatory signaling. Together, they establish STAT6 activation as the direct causal mechanism through which AV drives M2 macrophage polarization.
After selecting the appropriate constituents for the composite bioink, the optimization of their respective proportions was performed through a systematic multi-parametric evaluation balancing printability, structural fidelity, mechanical properties, and post-printing cell viability. Printability was quantified through filament extrusion continuity, diffusion ratio (Dfr), and the printability coefficient (Pr). Cell survival was assessed via Live/Dead staining and CCK-8 proliferation assays on encapsulated BMSCs, while structural robustness was determined by measuring compressive Young’s modulus. Each constituent’s concentration was optimized based on defined trade-offs: GelMA at 10 wt% provided the baseline cell-adhesive hydrogel network; lower concentrations resulted in weak mechanical support and structural collapse, while higher concentrations restricted cell migration and matrix remodeling. Laponite at 1 wt% acted as the key rheological driver; its “house-of-cards” microstructure imparted strong shear-thinning behavior, elevating shape fidelity (Pr ≈ 1.0), whereas higher Laponite loading caused nozzle clogging and elevated shear stress that reduced cell viability below 80%. AV at 40 vol% supplied the optimal threshold of bioactive polysaccharides (e.g., acemannan) for robust, long-term M2 macrophage polarization; lower AV fractions weakened immunomodulatory efficacy, whereas higher AV fractions over-diluted the precursor solution and compromised photo-cross-linking structural integrity. Consequently, the final optimized formulation of GelMA:Laponite:AV = 10%:2%:40% with a BMSCs density of 1 × 106 cells/mL was selected as the sweet spot, yielding continuous filament deposition, precise 3D architecture, and superior cell viability exceeding 90%.
These constituents may contribute to macrophage regulation and tissue repair.11 Indeed, acemannan alone was sufficient to drive complete M2 conversion of bone marrow macrophages (Liu and Chen, 2019, "Acemannan-driven M2 macrophage polarization accelerates calvarial bone healing").
